post_details: Hello friends, I'm simulating an animation of a girl swimming in her clothes, at a certain moment she is sucked and this causes the movement to be very accelerated in a specific part of the animation. This is causing an error that I have noticed before in other simulations and that I call a teleport error. I call this error like that because the movement is so fast that I think Marvelous cannot interpret that passage (as if instead of a movement we had a teleportation). Attached is a photo for you to understand. I'm simulating at 24 fps, and I've tried to lower the timestep to 0.010416 and the problem still hasn't been resolved. Does anyone know of a way to resolve this type of problem?

comments.comment_body: To run a simulation at an unusual speed, I would recommend running the animation at a slower speed than it originally was, just so Marvelous Designer can calculate the movements of the clothes. Once you have the animation you want, you can change the parameters of the animation itself (In this case the Speed) in the software you are working on once you export your MD clothing animations. I can see that the error is generated from frames 64 to 66. Among them, there are no references in terms of movement so that MD can understand the movement of the avatar itself to make the modifications to the clothes. The error takes place in 0.125 seconds (3 frames). It's too fast even for a real-world scenario. Try as I just said, adjusting the speed, perform the simulation, then once you have the simulation in your preferred third-party software, edit the speed of the animation to your liking (Super Fast in this case). This will allow you to have those frames that will give coherence to the movement of the avatar to be able to simulate. Best regards, Marvelous Designer Support Team

post_title: Request for improved timestep calculation based on FPS changes
post_details: Hello, I have been struggling for an hour with the simulation properties while simulating clothes on an alembic. I have found that the documentation for timesteps is not very clear, or perhaps nonexistent... Here is my understanding: I have been simulating with 25 frames per second (FPS) animation, and by default, MD has 30 FPS. According to MD, the timestep was set to 0.033 (the math for 1 second/30 FPS = 0.0333). Therefore, in practice, I need to manually change my FPS to 25 and then calculate the timesteps. I have done the math myself, which I will share below in case anyone needs it: 1 substep per frame: 0.04 seconds 2 substeps per frame: 0.02 seconds 4 substeps per frame: 0.01 seconds 8 substeps per frame: 0.005 seconds 16 substeps per frame: 0.0025 seconds 32 substeps per frame: 0.00125 seconds My request to the developers is the following: I believe that you can significantly improve our lives, you gorgeous wizards! How about MD computes timestep count by itself according to FPS changes in the project? So artists can only input the number of substeps they want for one frame. For example, we would only write the number 8 for substeps, and MD would look at the framerate of the project and convert timesteps accordingly. Thank you very much! I love your product, and I believe we will see this feature in the future. Best regards, Baji

comments.comment_body: 1 substep per frame: 0.04 seconds 2 substeps per frame: 0.02 seconds 4 substeps per frame: 0.01 seconds 8 substeps per frame: 0.005 seconds 16 substeps per frame: 0.0025 seconds 32 substeps per frame: 0.00125 seconds
Thanks for leaving this feedback to us. We will review this and share with dev team.

post_title: Arragement Points - Automatic Generation - Feature Request
post_details: Hi, It's possible to automaticly create arrangement points / bounding volumes for a custom Avartar (human biped)? If not I would like to leave that feature request. Using the Fitting Suit feature looks like it should be easy to reuse that data and adapt to automatic arrangement points!? Thnak you, André

comments.comment_body: When importing a custom avatar, the size of your avatar must be adjusted to the size of our avatars. This will allow it to fit existing arrangement points which you can modify to better fit the anatomy of the custom avatar. You can adjust it on Avatar - Avatar Editor - Arrangement. It is not possible to do an automatic conversion of the arrangement points on import. Auto Fitting Suite will create an approximation to the human anatomical distribution, but it will not allow to create a distribution of the different parts of the body from it, as not all custom avatars share the same distribution. Best regards, Marvelous Designer Support Team

post_details: Hello there, I kinda new in this field and while experimenting, I came across a little problem (see pictures below). I've tried a lot of things : either it becomes worse or it doesn't change anything. Any suggestion about how to fix it?

comments.comment_body: One of two causes, depending on where on the torso this is happening. 1. If this is happening on the lower back at the waistlin, then this is an issue called "swayback". You will need to make a horizontal dart across the back to remove the excess material. Here is a video explaining the swayback correction for patterns: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rODiDoenH7I 2. If this is happening at random places on the waist, then it could be that your lower torso patterns are too tight on the avatar, and are riding up to a position of less strain, and thus bunching up at the waist. Use the Slash+Spread tool to swing the lower hem a bit wider. It's hard to tell for sure which will be the correct answer, as your screenshots are clipped a bit tight, removing some of the overall information that might have been deduced.
Hello. It was a "swayback" problem. There were also sewing length problems, I've changed the pattern, starting from scratch with a new one. It's fixed now. Thanks for the hint.

comments.comment_body: Thank you for contracting us, To change the cloth physical property, select the fabric and under property editor, go to Physical Property and click the drop down arrow under Preset. To make the fabric less stretchy and less bendy, increase the number for Stretch and Bending. You can also chose the "Trim_Full_Grain_leather" fabric preset, which is a very strong fabric. To make it less affected by gravity, you can try decreasing the number for density: You should also apply solidify to your bracelet. Please check out our tutorial on solidify here: [LINK]. Solidify can also be applied uniformly to the pattern piece by selecting the pattern, in the property editor, check the solidify check box: You can also use the tack tools to constraint the bracelet to the avatar body. comments.comment_body: Hi!! I'm by no means an expert. But maybe i can help a little. In terms of where to start there are many approaches but here is what i would do. The overall big shape is kinda like a tight turtleneck t-shirt where the arms, back and a bit of the chest area is cut out. So on pinterest I would look for either a basic tutleneck or t-shirt pattern and use that to cut out the shapes or use the basic marvelous t-shirt and tighten it around your avatar and extrude the neck to a turtleneck. then i would just cut away the pieces. Freeze the turtleneck into place since that piece is kinda consistence. cut out the arms+back part and readjust as needed. then i'd cut out the chestpiece and readjust again. then you could start attaching the straps and pockets and work on the hems for the bottom and zipper pieces and the side pieces on the triangle. now this is where the question is if you gonna stay in marvelous or is you gonna sculpt/model the details. if you gonna stay within marvelous there are a lot of youtube tutorials where they show how to attach zippers and those rings (sorry i'm also still learning those so i'm not quite sure about that workflow) or sculpt them since those rings are easily modeled and there are zipper brushes. I hope this helps a little bit - idk if that is the right way to approach it but i think thats how i would. lemme know if you want more help - and i'm down to jump to a quick discord call or sth!

comments.comment_body: Thank you for contacting us, You do not need to hold shift if you are using the M:N sewing tool. Here's what you need to do: Click on all of the the segments belong to M segments. Then, hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete M sewing lines. M sewing lines are highlighted in neon color. As checking the Directional Notches, establish Sewing Lines on N segments. Then, hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete. If you have crisscross lines, it is most likely that your sewing direction is reversed. Please check the Directional Notches, and see if both the M and N side, the notches are at the side where you want the sewing to start. Let me know if you still have this issue after trying these. comments.comment_body: Here is the "magic formula" for autofitting. in short: you can't have autofitting without pre-existing reference data and to do that---you must apply that reference data to everything --- to be able to use "autofitting". (we have this template on the Discord channel) Hopefully this will help you with your issue: Getting errors with the Auto fitting and Target Re-Draping? Both avatars (the donor/original garment (A1) and the target avatar (A2)) NEED to have a fit suit created and saved, before the Autofit tool(s) can be used. The avatar the garment was first created on needs to have a Fit Suit created and saved as a part of the avatar's file (A1), and the avatar you want to put the garment on also needs a Fit suit created and saved (A2). Then the donor garment MUST be simulated on the donor (original) avatar (A1) and obtain Fit Suit Data (FSD), saved then that garment or file shared with the target avatar file (A2). If either of the avatars do not have the Fit Suit information saved in their file, the Autofit &amp Target Re-draping tools will not proceed. Working order: 1. A1 &amp A2 MUST have a Fitting suit EACH. (do NOT move to step 2 until BOTH have a fit suit.) 2. Simulate garment on A1 &gt save garment. You must save after simulation in order to have Garment with fit suit data (FSD) &gt Garment has FSD 3. Add Garment with FSD to project with A2. You can now use the autofitting tools. Checklist 1. Does the garment not have fit suit data? Garment not re-target draping or autofitting? Getting an error saying It only works for simulated garments? (if any apply: simulate garment on a V2 avatar to quickly apply fit suit data you might have to place it by hand) 2. Getting errors "it only works on avatars registered in advance"? Does the target avatar (the one you want to use aka A2) have a fit suit yet?(Fix: Make a fit suit on the target Avatar using the fit-suit tool in the 3D window) (for better formatting, here is the link to the discord channel/ exact post, you must join our discord to read it https://discord.com/channels/443279790808629259/824729101931642990/1016777079351685230)

comments.comment_body: OK, luckily it's an easy fix. Those are not basic jeans from our library, those are made by an artist on CONNECT MARKETPLACE who is not related to the company: so please note that anything not from any of the official accounts are not considered basic, or a part of our library. Those you have found are specifically made in CLO3D and are real functioning patterns, so lucky its a good place to start but because its a real garment you will need to work to place them on your avatar that it might not actually fit. Also consider that it has items in that scene that are optimized for real item production, has lots of small parts and is not made for 3D pipeline productions (has too many pieces). You will want to learn the basics of how layering, cloth simulation and how to stabilize your projects for working in a 3D pipeline. Basically: you always have to settle the fabric appropriately on any custom avatar, and you should expect that anything from a marketplace will need to be adjusted. Layer and fix your pockets based on how they exist in space (pockets below pants, pant above etc) Here is some videos on how layering works and how pants are layered in general: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bru4YNoHe4Q https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V-bajQpPGjU&amplist=PLYQUdblF9eDVOfLxK4WiDp2TU8O8ZeB8a https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rl-oPys2jtU&amplist=PLYQUdblF9eDU66lW8rnPRFXktPELWgWUX

post_title: Automatic created fitting suits at avatar upload in MD12 fails
post_details: Hi MD I have an issue with my Avatars that I am bringing into MD12. Id very much like to have them working with the new auto fitting suit creation at avatar upload but I seem to run into the same issue again and again no matter what I do. My Avatars are originally for Second Life. The Avatar is by default in several pieces in Blender but I merge them all into one full body mesh before I export. I make sure the avatar is the correct size by comparing it to the size of one of the inbuild avatars (Feifei) - mine is a tad bit larger but she is still under 2 meters so I should be good regarding that I think. The SL avatar is in T-pose and that seems to break the attachment points. If i move her to A-pose before export from Blender the attachment points works, but the auto fitting suit creation breaks in both scenarios. I have tried importing as fbx, collada and obj, all give me the same results where the auto fitting suit breaks (and often the attachment points too). The error message is always the same: "Avatar must be in a T-pose or A-pose" both where the attachment points and the fitting suit fails. The auto fitting suit fails just before "Synchronization complete". I tried with T-pose and with A-pose for the avatar before export out of Blender. I tried with and without including the armature when exporting from Blender. I am able to get the avatar into MD with the armature working - but it does not seem to make a difference whether its there or not regarding the auto fitting suit creation failing. I tried scaling the avatar smaller (down to 150 cm) to make certain its under 2 meters tall. Still it did not work. I noticed her feet are somewhat under the base plane when she has high heel foot shape. So I tried move her up a bit to have her above the plane - that made no difference either. I have experimented with deleting vertex groups and applying armature modifier and setting rest pose to A-pose/T-pose in Blender before export and of course i make sure to apply transforms as well. I am running out of ideas on what might affect this, although I am pretty sure it must be something carrying over from Blender before I import to MD12. A couple of days of testing any scenario I could think off and researching the internet for anyone facing this has given me no results so now I give in and ask for help here.
